what: Ingersoll Rand makes equipment that moves air and liquid: industrial compressors, vacuum pumps, blowers and precision pumps, plus specialised pumps for laboratories and life sciences. It grows largely by buying smaller makers of niche equipment.
customers: Manufacturers, chemical and food processors, pharmaceutical and laboratory customers, and energy companies.
money: compressors, vacuum pumps, blowers and aftermarket parts
precision pumps for life sciences and medical use
moat: Compressors installed in factories that then need parts and service for twenty years, delivered through a distribution network that competitors cannot easily replicate.
risks: Industrial capital spending has been soft in Europe and China
Debt of about $5 billion funds that programme
Return on invested capital of about 6% reflects goodwill from past deals
opportunities: Revenue grew about 6% last year with a 44% gross margin
Aftermarket parts and service are around a third of revenue and far steadier than new equipment
Life science pumps serve a market growing faster than general industry
watch: Organic order growth and aftermarket revenue share.
